intro: Standard 7 of the Care Certificate covers protecting people's privacy and dignity in everyday care, and the law and frameworks behind them.
points: Privacy and dignity are legal duties under Human Rights Act Article 8 and CQC Regulation 10, not optional extras or personal style.
During personal care, knock and wait, close doors and curtains, and cover the person, exposing only the part you are caring for.
Keep personal information confidential, sharing only on a need-to-know basis; but confidentiality is not secrecy — share to protect someone from serious harm.
Uphold dignity in small things: use preferred names, avoid childish language, do not rush, and speak to people rather than over them.
Respect dignity of risk: people with capacity may make unwise choices, so support informed decisions rather than removing all risk.
Offer real choice and active participation, doing things with people not for them, and challenge or report any undignified practice you see.
